name: nema17_mount_research
description: Research-grounded lightweight part — the prompt names a standard product (NEMA 17 stepper) WITHOUT its interface dims. agent_research=auto must fire on the NEMA token, the pre-intake research step grounds the real mounting interface (pilot bore dia 22, 4x M3 screws on the 31 mm square = PCD 43.8), intake lands the sourced facts in spec.assumptions (spec_contains asserts 'researched:' evidence), and the generated mount must match the real NEMA dims — geometry gates check the interface, not just self-consistency.

stages.prompt:
Lightweight upright mount for a NEMA 17 stepper motor (FDM print). mm.

A compact L-bracket standing on its foot flange:
1. Vertical square face plate, ~4 mm thick — the stepper's front face bolts
   onto it. Cut the motor's real front-face interface exactly: the pilot
   recess bore and the 4-hole bolt pattern, both as through-holes sized to
   clear the motor's own screws. Both open on the face that takes the motor;
   the bolt pattern is centred on the pilot.
2. Horizontal foot flange at the bottom edge, ~4 mm thick and ~20 mm deep,
   carrying two dia 4.5 mm through-holes about 30 mm apart — the bracket
   screws onto a frame edge through them.

Keep it light: just the two plates and the declared features — no ribs,
pockets, fillets or extra cutouts. The part must sit flat on the foot
flange (min z = 0).

The motor interface dims are published spec facts — use the researched
values exactly, do not guess them.
